outcome: A misconfiguration and the runtime activity that exploited it appear together as one incident with a single supervisory timeline.
overview: A fintech usually ends up with cloud security split across tools that were each bought to answer one question: posture in one console, workload alerts in another, runtime detections somewhere else. Cortex Cloud brings posture and cloud detection and response into one place, so a misconfiguration and the runtime activity that exploited it appear as one story. For a regulated fintech the argument is as much about evidence as detection — a supervisor asking what happened wants a timeline, not three exports that have to be aligned by hand.

benefits.text: Posture findings and runtime detections are correlated rather than held in separate consoles
benefits.limits: Correlation depends on both sides being onboarded; a partial rollout produces the same fragmentation under a new name

benefits.text: An incident in cloud can be reconstructed as one timeline for a supervisor or an auditor
benefits.limits: Timeline completeness is bounded by retention purchased and by which accounts were onboarded at the time of the event

benefits.text: Consolidating tools reduces the number of consoles a small security team has to operate
benefits.limits: The control plane is vendor-operated, so tenant region and log residency are design decisions to be made and recorded explicitly rather than properties of the product

residency: Vendor-operated control plane; detection telemetry and findings leave the customer tenancy, and the tenant region is chosen and recorded at design

notFor.situation: An organisation with a tuned cloud detection capability in an existing platform
notFor.why: Detection content and tuning accumulate value that does not port, and consolidation resets it

notFor.situation: An estate small enough that one provider’s native tooling covers it
notFor.why: Consolidation solves a fragmentation problem; where there is no fragmentation it adds a platform

scope:
Model: Redington solutions engineering with an accredited Palo Alto Networks implementation partner · Duration: 10–14 weeks to posture and runtime onboarded with tuned detection on the first tranche
Support model: Vendor subscription support; Redington coordinates the vendor case. Optional managed triage against an agreed alert-quality target.
1) Assessment — tooling overlap, account and workload counts, timeline-production baseline, residency position
2) Design — retention per data class, detection content tranches, tenant region and alert-quality threshold
3) Onboard — posture and runtime for the first account tranche, first content tranche enabled
4) Consolidate and hand over — remaining accounts onboarded, overlapping tools identified for retirement, operations handed over
